chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'a said: Wuhayb narrated to them from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"Any man who has sexual intercourse with a slave woman of a people unlawfully, then buys her and claims her child, he is not inherited from him. For the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The child belongs to the bed (of the father), and for the fornicator is the stone.' So the child of fornication is not inherited from, except by a man who claims the child of his slave girl."

key_terms.اَلْوَلَدُ لِلْفِرَاشِ: The child belongs to the bed (legitimate father)

ai.seo_question: What is the inheritance ruling for a man who has illicit relations with a slave woman and then buys her?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration to clarify the inheritance rights of a man who consummates illicit relations with a slave woman and subsequently purchases her. The ruling hinges on the Prophetic maxim 'The child belongs to the bed' (*al-waladu lil-firash*), which prioritizes the marital context for lineage; thus, unless the man explicitly claims the child as his own from his specific slave girl, the child does not inherit from him. This highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on clear paternity claims (*iqrar*) in cases of *ilhad* (illegitimate offspring) to determine inheritance shares.
